title: NetworkStatus
description:
The machine's wired network interfaces, and any change on trial.

The owner, 2026-10-19: "Network Settings via Admin GUI, also ob DHCP/Static inkl IP Subnetz Gateway DNS etc." — and on the safety net, five minutes to confirm before the previous settings come back by themselves.

interfaces.description: Every wired interface, in name order. Not the loopback, not a VPN and not a radio: none of those is configured here.

nameservers.description: The nameservers the machine uses now, whichever interface set them.

trial.description: The last change and where it got, if one has ever been made here.

unavailable.description: Why nothing can be changed from here, where nothing can: a machine whose network is not run by `ifupdown` is changed where it is run.

NetworkInterface.description: One wired interface, as it is and as it is configured.

addresses.description: The IPv4 addresses it has now, as `address/prefix`.

configured.description: The configured static settings, where the method is `static`.

gateway.description: The default gateway through it now, if there is one.

link.description: Whether a cable with something at the other end is plugged in.

method.description: How it is configured to come up: `dhcp`, `static`, or `none` where the configuration does not mention it.

speed_mbps.description: The link's speed in megabits a second, where the driver says.

NetworkSettings.description: Settings for one interface: the request to change them, and what a static configuration holds.

gateway.description: The default gateway, for `static`. Optional: a show network often has none.

netmask.description: The subnet mask, as `255.255.255.0` or as a prefix length such as `24`.

NetworkTrial.description:
A change to the network, and how far it got.

Written by the machine's own network helper, which runs apart from the server: it has to be able to put the previous settings back when nobody can reach the server any more.

at.description: When it last wrote this, as UTC in ISO 8601.

deadline.description: When the previous settings come back by themselves, in seconds since the epoch, while it is `waiting`.

detail.description: What it is doing, or why it stopped, in a sentence.

stage.description: `applying`, `waiting` for somebody to keep it, then `kept`, `restored`, `failed` or `refused`.

summary.description: What it set, in a few words: `static 10.110.0.50/24` or `dhcp`.
